Stream Commands

Usage: whizbang streams purge [options]

Removes durable streams that should never have existed from one service's store: events, every
perspective's rows, perspective work, cursors and snapshots, outbox, inbox and deduplication entries.
One transaction per batch; each batch is audited, and the streams stay purged: a later event on one
is skipped by every perspective. Stop whatever produces events for the streams first.

Options:
  --connection, -c <string>   PostgreSQL connection string of the service's database
  --schema, -s <name>         The schema the service uses (default: public)
  --reason, -r <text>         Why, recorded in the audit (required)
  --requested-by, -u <name>   Who, recorded in the audit (default: the OS user)
  --stream <id>               A stream to purge (repeatable)
  --streams-file, -f <path>   A file of stream ids, one per line ('#' comments)
  --dry-run                   Report the rows per table that would go, and change nothing
  --batch-size, -b <n>        Streams per transaction (default: 100)
  --purge-id, -p <guid>       Resume an earlier purge:

Audit Command

Usage: whizbang audit [options]

Checks the Whizbang package versions a project resolves (transitive ones included) against the
published security advisories in the OSV database (https://api.osv.dev), the same data NuGet
Audit and Dependabot read. Run it after dotnet restore. Requests are anonymous.

Options:
  --project, -p <path>   A project file, a .sln or .slnx solution, or a directory searched
                         for projects (default: the current directory)
  --fail-on <level>      low | moderate | high | critical | none (default: moderate)
  --timeout <seconds>    Give up on OSV after this long (default: 15)
  --json                 Write the report as JSON
  --help, -h             Show this help

Exit codes:
  0  No advisory at or above --fail-on
  1  At least one advisory at or above --fail-on
  2  Could not check: no restore output, OSV unreachable or too slow, or bad arguments

Examples:
  whizbang audit
  whizbang audit --project ./MyService.slnx --fail-on high
  whizbang audit --json > audit.json

Stream Commands

Usage: whizbang streams purge [options]

Removes durable streams that should never have existed from one service's store: events, every
perspective's rows, perspective work, cursors and snapshots, outbox, inbox and deduplication entries.
One transaction per batch; each batch is audited, and the streams stay purged: a later event on one
is skipped by every perspective. Stop whatever produces events for the streams first.

Options:
  --connection, -c <string>   PostgreSQL connection string of the service's database
  --schema, -s <name>         The schema the service uses (default: public)
  --reason, -r <text>         Why, recorded in the audit (required)
  --requested-by, -u <name>   Who, recorded in the audit (default: the OS user)
  --stream <id>               A stream to purge (repeatable)
  --streams-file, -f <path>   A file of stream ids, one per line ('#' comments)
  --dry-run                   Report the rows per table that would go, and change nothing
  --batch-size, -b <n>
